title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
layout_note: The overview on the left (about 40% of the width) sits on a loose 2x2 grid: Retriever top-left, the retrieved documents top-right, the test context bottom-left, the black-box LM bottom-right. From the context, one branch goes up to the Retriever, right to the documents and down into the LM; a second branch runs straight right into the LM; the LM's output drops below it. The right ~60% is one detail panel that expands the 'Input Reformulation' step and is tied to it by a speech-bubble pointer. Inside the panel the flow is three parallel left-to-right rows that a curly brace merges into one chart.
grouping: The overview has no containers; its four parts are separated by space only. The detail panel is a large borderless pale-yellow rounded rectangle labelled 'Ensemble' below its rows, holding three identical rows stacked vertically under shared column headers (d_i above the document boxes, x above the context boxes). Colour families carry identity across both halves: light-blue boxes are always documents, light-grey boxes are always the test context, dark red marks retrieval (the Retriever block, the 'Document Retrieval' label, the variable symbols), and each of the three rows gets its own bar colour (green, purple, pink). A curly brace groups the three per-row bar charts and points to the merged chart.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with a generous corner radius. The Retriever is a solid dark-red block with large white sans-serif text and no outline; document boxes are light blue with a thin grey-blue outline and a soft drop shadow, and the retrieved document is drawn as three offset stacked cards. Context boxes are light grey with a darker grey outline and monospace text; in the panel each document box abuts its context box so the pair reads as one joined input. The LM is a black 3-D cube with white edge lines and an orange question mark on its front face, repeated smaller in each panel row. Overview arrows are thick medium-grey shafts with filled heads; panel arrows are thin black. The bar charts are unlabelled horizontal bars on a vertical baseline with faint vertical gridlines, category words (apple, pear, not, ...) right-aligned to the left; the merged chart stacks the three row colours as segments within each bar.
proposed_highlight: The two method steps are named by bold italic arrow labels rather than boxes: 'Document Retrieval' in dark red beside the upward arrow (the same red as the Retriever block) and 'Input Reformulation' in orange beside the arrow into the LM. The Retriever is the only solid saturated block in the figure. The reformulation step is expanded into the yellow detail panel through a speech-bubble pointer, and the LM is drawn as an opaque black cube with a question mark and the monospace label 'Black-box LM'.
lesson: The ensemble is drawn as data, not as an operator box: each pass gets its own bar colour, and a curly brace gathers the three bar charts into one stacked chart whose segments keep those colours, so each document's contribution stays visible in the merged result.
notes: elements 'other' = the dark-red italic math symbols (x, d_i) used as box tags and column headers, and the three-card document stack. Fonts split by role: sans-serif for names and document text, monospace for the test context, the 'Black-box LM' label and the red output word 'Apple'. Venue NAACL as recorded (venue_source semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2301.12652), the venue year was not verified. The whole figure is one embedded raster (the recorded image box covers the full crop), so kb measure cannot separate embedded images: photo_share is null.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: retrieval augmentation for black-box LMs via ensembling

core.what: a dark-red Retriever block left of the main flow sends light-blue stacked document cards (with real text) down into the black-box LM, which the grey test-context box enters from the left

relations.form: Test Context box -> up arrow 'Document Retrieval' -> Retriever -> right arrow -> a stack of three light-blue document cards with real sentences, then a down arrow into the LM cube
the document arrow from above and the test-context arrow from the left converge on one black cube labelled Black-box LM, which outputs 'Apple' below
a pale-yellow rounded 'Ensemble' panel on the right, attached by a speech-bubble pointer at the 'Input Reformulation' label, expands the LM step

inside the panel, three identical rows each prepend a different document d_i (blue card) to the same context x (grey card), feed an identical black cube and end in a small bar chart over apple/pear/not
a right curly brace gathers the three per-row bar charts into one stacked bar chart whose segments keep each row's colour (green, purple, pink)

channels.colour: fill = kind of data: light blue = retrieved document, grey = test context, black cube = the frozen LM; bar colour = which document the probability came from; dark red marks both the Retriever block and the math labels d_i and x, so red carries 'retrieval' and 'variable name' at once
channels.shape: rounded text cards = data with real text, black 3-D cube with a question mark = black-box model, bar charts = output distributions
channels.line: thick grey arrows in the overview, thin black arrows inside the ensemble panel; no line-style distinction of meaning
channels.frame: one tinted rounded panel = the expanded ensemble step; the overview is unframed

quality.strengths: documents and context are drawn as real sentences, and the per-document output distributions are drawn as bar charts, so what is ensembled is visible; the three ensemble rows are identical copies differing only in the document; the brace-to-stacked-bar merge shows the weighting as geometry
quality.weaknesses: the largest, most saturated element is the off-the-shelf Retriever (solid dark-red block) while the ensemble contribution sits in a pale panel; the speech-bubble tie to 'Input Reformulation' points at a label rather than at the LM node it expands; red is shared between the retriever and generic math symbols

insights.structure: Left ~40%: an unframed overview on a loose 2x2 grid (Retriever, retrieved documents, test context, black-box LM); right ~60%: a pale-yellow rounded 'Ensemble' panel expanding the Input Reformulation step, tied to the overview by a speech-bubble pointer.
insights.data: Documents are light-blue rounded boxes and the test context grey boxes with real example text; the LM is a black cube with an orange question mark; each of three rows ends in a small horizontal bar chart over apple/pear/not.
insights.emphasis: The Retriever is a solid dark-red block and retrieval labels are dark red, while the ensemble panel's per-row bar colours (green, purple, pink) are stacked into one merged chart via a curly brace.
insights.flow: Thick grey arrows: context up to Retriever, right to documents, down into the LM, output 'Apple' below; in the panel three parallel left-to-right rows converge through a brace to the merged distribution.

arrangement.units: unframed overview on the left; one tinted rounded detail panel on the right with three parallel rows
arrangement.inputs_as: grey box with the test context sentence
arrangement.shared: colour identity for documents (blue) and context (grey) across both halves
